transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Start: 10:30 AM ET
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Sophie Chen (Redwood AE), Mateo Alvarez (Redwood SE), Jordan Blake (ACME CISO), Priya Nair (ACME Head of IT), Liam O'Connor (ACME Infra), Samir Patel (ACME Sec Eng)

Summary (auto): quick posture review of SOC2/ISO artifacts, trust center access, RBAC/SSO and KMS options; action items assigned.

[00:00] Sophie (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Sophie, AE for ACME, with Mateo our SE. How's everybody doing?
[00:07] Jordan (ACME - CISO): Good, thanks. Busy week but glad we could get this on the calendar.
[00:12] Priya (ACME - Head IT): Morning.
[00:15] Mateo (Redwood SE): morning — quick agenda: we'll run through our SOC2 type II artifacts, ISO 27001 cert, how to get access to the trust center, then dig into RBAC/SSO, audit logs, data residency and KMS/BYOK options.
[00:28] Liam (ACME): That sounds good. We mainly want to validate controls and make sure there's an easy way to map our compliance matrix to Redwood.

[03:02] Sophie: Great — starting with the reports: Redwood holds a SOC 2 Type II for our hosted API and dedicated fleet, and we also maintain ISO 27001 certification for our control plane. We can provide the Type II report with redactions for customer-specific data.
[03:20] Jordan: When you say dedicated fleet, is that the Redwood Dedicated offering or the Private deployment?
[03:28] Mateo: good call — dedicated is our reserved capacity in the Redwood cloud, where customers get dedicated GPUs and isolation, but it's still Redwood managed. Private is the VPC/on-prem option where the control plane can be customer-managed; both are covered in the scope of the same SOC 2 program, though some deployment-specific controls differ.
[03:45] Priya: ok, do you have a controls mapping for customers to see which controls map to their own responsibilities?
[03:53] Sophie: yes — we maintain a controls mapping template we share in the trust center; it has the standard split: infrastructure, platform, customer config. We'll send the template and can walk through the mapping with you.

[06:12] Mateo: quick note on trust center access — we can provision a read-only link for your security team that contains the Type II report, ISO cert, penetration test summary, and our security policies. It's not a fully open portal, we create account access for folks you specify.
[06:30] Samir (ACME): we need at least two reviewers to see the raw log retention and encryption details — will that be in the trust center?
[06:38] Mateo: yes, the trust center has an artifacts folder with a log retention matrix, encryption at rest/in transit descriptions, and KMS options. If you need deeper artifacts we can do an NDA-exchange for some pen test outputs.

[09:00] Jordan: on encryption — do you support customer-managed keys? BYOK? HSM-backed KMS?
[09:06] Mateo: we support BYOK for Private deployments via customer KMS/HSM integration and we offer an envelope encryption model for Dedicated where you can bring your own KMS where supported. For hosted, we use Redwood-managed KMS but can negotiate B.Y.O.K. for enterprise contracts with HSM-backed keys.
[09:25] Priya: is there an option to rotate keys on schedule and have rotation logs surfaced?
[09:30] Mateo: yes, rotation events are logged in the audit trail; we can export those to your SIEM. Rotation schedules are customer-configurable in Private, and we can coordinate rotation windows for Dedicated with minimal downtime.

[11:55] Sophie: switching to RBAC and SSO — we support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM provisioning for user sync, and fine-grained RBAC with roles and token scopes. We also have organization-level and project-level roles.
[12:10] Jordan: do you support SCIM group sync to map our AD groups to Redwood roles?
[12:16] Mateo: yes, SCIM group sync is supported; mapping is flexible so you can map AD groups to Redwood role templates. Small caveat: some legacy SAML providers may need custom attribute mapping.
[12:30] Samir: how granular is the RBAC? can we restrict who can access keys, create rollouts, or read logs?
[12:36] Mateo: yes — we have granular permissions like admin, devops, billing, security-reader — you can separate key management permissions from deploy permissions. We also log access to secrets in the audit logs.

[15:05] Priya: audit logs — what is your default retention and can we export to Splunk/Datadog?
[15:12] Mateo: default is 90 days in the hosted product, but for enterprise contracts we can extend retention — commonly 365 days. We support streaming logs to SIEM via secure connectors (S3 + Kinesis or direct ingestion endpoints).
[15:28] Liam: and are those logs tamper-evident?
[15:31] Mateo: logs are signed and the system keeps immutable append-only storage; we can provide hash-based verification artifacts for critical windows if you need to validate integrity.

[18:40] Jordan: data residency question — can we guarantee EU-only processing for EU customers?
[18:46] Sophie: yes we have region controls; you can pin workloads to EU regions for data residency. For Dedicated we can provision capacity in region; for Private, obviously the data stays in your VPC or on-prem. Note that metadata in the control plane may still be stored in the control plane region unless you run Private with a customer-managed control plane.
[19:10] Priya: backups — where are backups stored and encrypted?
[19:14] Mateo: backups are encrypted at rest with KMS, stored in region-aligned object storage; for cross-region DR we do encrypted replication but only with customer approval for sensitive regulated customers.

[22:02] Samir: audit for SOC2 – are there any open exceptions in the latest Type II?
[22:08] Sophie: no open exceptions in the current cycle; there were two low-risk findings in 2025 that were remediated and validated. We'll include the remediation detail in the redacted report.

[24:45] Mateo: controls mapping process: we usually share a spreadsheet template, you fill in current state for each control, and we mark who owns the control (ACME vs Redwood) and provide evidence links. We can drive the initial pass with you and iterate.
[24:58] Jordan: that's the part we want to tackle — can you assign someone to help?
[25:03] Sophie: yes I'll own the mapping coordination and Mateo will help on technical evidence for infra-related controls.

[27:30] Priya: legal/procurement will want the standard contract language on liability/incident response — do you publish an incident response SLA?
[27:38] Sophie: yes we have incident response procedures and SLAs depending on your tier; we can share a redacted incident playbook and include our notification timelines in the contract exhibit.

[30:12] Liam: SIEM integration specifics — what formats do you export logs in, and do you support syslog?
[30:19] Mateo: we export JSON event streams to S3 and can provide a Kinesis stream for near-real-time ingestion; syslog can be supported via a connector but typically we recommend S3/Kinesis to avoid fleet-level NAT issues. We'll share example log schemas.

[33:04] Samir: for private deployments, how does the KMS integration work — do you require a VPN or private link?
[33:11] Mateo: for Private, we support direct KMS connections over customer network, and we can use PrivateLink or VPC peering. For on-prem HSMs, we do a secure tunnel and mTLS-authenticated API calls for encryption operations.
[33:28] Jordan: any impact to latency when using remote KMS?
[33:32] Mateo: minimal; we use envelope encryption to avoid per-request KMS roundtrips. Only key unwraps happen during session establishment; the per-token generation path does not call KMS per token.

[36:00] Sophie: quick note on model telemetry — we collect anonymized usage metrics for performance tuning; customer content is not used to train models unless contractually agreed.
[36:10] Priya: need that in writing — acceptable use policy and data processing addendum.
[36:16] Sophie: absolutely, we have a DPA and Acceptable Use Policy in the trust center; we'll include that in the artifact bundle.

[38:40] Jordan: are there certifications or attestations for the underlying GPU host provider?
[38:46] Mateo: yes, our cloud partners maintain their own certifications and we can provide their compliance docs as third-party attestations; for Dedicated we also have controls that map to vendor security.

[41:12] Priya: outstanding question — could you provide sample evidence for network segmentation and change control?
[41:18] Mateo: yes, we can export network architecture diagrams and change control logs from our ticketing system as redacted artifacts; again those live in the trust center for approved viewers.

[43:30] Sophie: to recap next steps: I'll send the SOC2 Type II and ISO cert by Friday, Mateo will provision trust center access and send an invite, we'll share controls mapping template and set a follow-up for KMS deep dive the week of Mar 16.
[43:50] Jordan: perfect. Also we want the retention rows for logs and specific SIEM schema by next check-in.
[43:58] Liam: and please include any sample rotation logs for keys so we can validate rotation events.
[44:05] Sophie: noted — Samir, Priya, Jordan we'll cc you on the artifacts.

[45:30] Mateo: any final questions?
[45:35] Priya: no, that's all for now.
[45:38] Jordan: thank you both.
[45:40] Sophie: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts and a calendar invite for the technical deep dive.
[45:47] Meeting end: 11:17 AM ET

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and speaker overlap; some technology names abbreviated.
